data.cultural_impact: The name Jasvant carries a sense of triumph and victory, reflecting Hindu ideals of personal success and progress. This name is often given to children born into families who have endured hardships or have faced obstacles, as a reminder of their inherent potential for overcoming challenges and achieving greatness.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the name Jasvant carries deep spiritual meaning. It is believed that the divine brings victory and success in one's spiritual journey. The name is a reminder that one's inner strength and connection to God can help overcome any obstacle or challenge, and lead to spiritual enlightenment and inner peace. It is a name that inspires one to strive for personal growth and to look to the divine for guidance and support.

historical_references.reference: Jasvant was a famous Jain Tirthankara of the 12th Jain Tirthankara cycle, known as the Siddhantakala. He is believed to have lived approximately between 372-361 BCE.

Jasvant is also mentioned in various Indian literary works, including the 11th century Jain text, 'Parishishtaparvan'. He is described as a ruler of a small kingdom in the region of Rajasthan and is believed to have renounced his royal duties and become an ascetic.
